purpose: Shared conformance vectors for ntfy header sanitisation. HTTP header values are ByteStrings (latin-1): Node/undici THROWS and Python requests/urllib RAISE UnicodeEncodeError for any codepoint > 255, killing primary AND fallback identically before a socket opens. curl/bash is unaffected (it sends raw bytes). Every fleet publisher in a throwing language MUST run its local implementation against these vectors in CI, so divergence fails a build instead of losing a page.
semantics: transliterate-then-fold-then-degrade: map known Unicode punctuation to ASCII, strip CR/LF, fold accented letters to their ASCII base via NFKD, then replace any residual non-ASCII with '?'. Output is PURE ASCII. This is stricter than latin-1 on purpose: httpx encodes headers as ASCII and raises UnicodeEncodeError on 'e-acute', where urllib and Node accept it. ASCII is the only safe common denominator across the fleet's HTTP clients. Combining marks are DROPPED (not degraded), so NFD-decomposed input folds identically to NFC. Characters with no NFKD decomposition but an obvious ASCII rendering (ss, ae, o, deg, u, 1/2) are transliterated explicitly.
never_sanitize: Authorization (a bearer is ASCII by construction; mangling it turns an encoding bug into an auth bug)
the message BODY (sent as UTF-8; may hold any character)
